summary: Fossil size data exist for both groups (PBDB: 97 Meganisoptera occurrences and 110 meganeurid measurements; Dryad n0310 pterosaur size compilation), and Phanerozoic CO2 is compiled openly (Paleo-CO2 archive, GEOCARB in NOAA). The variable the explanation actually needs, total atmospheric density/pressure in the Carboniferous and Jurassic, has no proxy dataset in these archives (NOAA 'atmospheric pressure' hits are Quaternary ice cores), and paired wingspan–body-mass tables for the giant insects are in paper supplements rather than repositories.
next_step: Compile wingspan and mass estimates for Meganeuridae and Jurassic pterosaurs from PBDB measurements plus literature supplements (Clapham & Karr 2012; Witton 2008 pterosaur masses), pair with Paleo-CO2 and published O2 curves, and treat total pressure as a modelled parameter with stated bounds rather than a dataset.
obstacles_confirmed: Ancient total atmospheric pressure is poorly constrained (no repository proxy dataset found).
Carbon dioxide concentration is not total air density or pressure, which is what the flight calculation uses.
Many specimens lack paired wingspan and body mass.
